items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: I said Joe Glager. He said who's Joe Glager? I said, Joe Glager's the one that owned the band.

ctx.x: I say, yeah, I got everyone, which I did. Had all of them, so he says, okay, I'll tell you what I'll do for you. He said I'll call the head office downtown and they can have a date for you and you go down there and you tell them the whole bit. I said, okay, so they called me and then he said -- I forget the day, but he said you go on down there, he says, ask for Mr. So-and-so, and he'll take care of you.

So I went down there with all my receipts, he said take all your receipts, took all of them. I went down there and he even had the deduction for unemployment and social security and all that, so this fellow down there, we started talking and he asked me for the receipts and I give him the whole bunch of them, he said, my God, what's all this? So he says -- says who's your boss? I said Joe Glager. He said who's Joe Glager? I said, Joe Glager's the one that owned the band. Say, well isn't Louis Armstrong the leader?

I say, yeah, he's just the leader, but he doesn't hire the band, he -- all he can do is fire them and he can't do that until he tells Joe Glager he don't want them. So that's the way they get fired. He said, but he's the leader, why, what -- so he says why isn't his name on here? He's the leader -- I say I don't know. He said we'll find out, so they got a disc and they're talking and I'm telling them all this so they said, okay, you'll hear from us.

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: he sold Louie to Joe Glaser for $500, I think it was.

ctx.x: Did he meet Louie in Chicago?

He bought Louie from a guy that beat Louie on the boat that had Louie under contract. And coming back he didn't want to be bothered with Louie again -- they had an argument or something and they had a fight. So when they came back to the states, see, he sold Louie to Joe Glaser for $500, I think it was.

And Glaser was a go-getter. He went on the road with -- he was the manager then with Louie playing these southern gigs. And Louie used to tell him how they was all so scared because them crackers was giving Joe hell because he was a Jew and working with the Negroes, and that did it, you know.
